original_question: Let C be the central Cantor set generated by the fast convergent geometric sequence (q^n) with q in (0, 1/2), and let E(q^n) denote the adjoint Cantorval obtained by adjoining the gaps removed at odd-numbered steps. Compute the center of distances C(E(q^n)).
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 35: compute the center of distances of the adjoint Cantorval associated with the geometric central Cantor set (the odd-gap adjunction construction; the model Cantorval is the motivating example).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant family (geometric central Cantor sets), the correct derived object (the adjoint Cantorval obtained by adjoining the gaps removed at odd-numbered stages), and the actual task posed in the paper: to determine its center of distances.
missing_details: The paper’s operator is the center of distances on subsets of the real line, so the ambient metric space should be stated explicitly as (R,|·|).
The paper’s question is naturally quantified for each parameter q in the allowed geometric range, not just for an unspecified fixed example.
The generating Cantor set should be defined explicitly, e.g. C_q:=E((q^n)_{n>=1})={sum_{n>=1} eps_n q^n : eps_n in {0,1}} (or an equivalent normalized geometric-central-Cantor-set model).
The indexing convention n>=1 for the geometric sequence should be fixed.

The adjoint Cantorval should be defined explicitly via the stagewise deleted-gap sets: if G_n is the union of the open intervals removed at stage n of the standard construction of C_q, then A_q:=C_q union (union over k>=1 of G_{2k-1}).
The center of distances itself should be defined explicitly: S(A_q):={alpha>=0 : for every x in A_q there exists y in A_q with |x-y|=alpha}.
Your notation C(E(q^n)) does not match the notation used in the center-of-distances literature around this paper, where S(·) is standard; the refined question should avoid that ambiguity.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should say that the goal is to determine the full set S(A_q), not merely to show inclusion or nontriviality.
If one wants to stay maximally paper-faithful, one should note that the model Cantorval is the odd-gap adjunction example and serves as the prototype for this problem.
refined_question: For each q in (0,1/2), let C_q:=E((q^n)_{n>=1})={sum_{n=1}^infinity eps_n q^n : eps_n in {0,1}} subset R, let G_n be the union of the open intervals removed at the n-th step in the standard construction of the central Cantor set C_q from [0,q/(1-q)], and define its adjoint Cantorval by A_q:=C_q union (union over k>=1 of G_{2k-1}) (so the case q=1/3 gives the model Cantorval up to the chosen normalization). Determine exactly the center of distances S(A_q):={alpha>=0 : for every x in A_q there exists y in A_q with |x-y|=alpha}.
justification: The draft is aiming at the open problem stated in Section 7 immediately after the paper defines the adjoint Cantorval: compute the center of distances of that odd-gap-adjoined Cantorval. The nearby context makes clear that the object is the adjoint Cantorval of a central Cantor set, with the model Cantorval as the basic example, and that the problem is genuinely parameterized by q in the geometric case. Your draft is close, but it leaves implicit the ambient metric, the exact definitions of the generating Cantor set and of the adjoint Cantorval, the full quantifier over q, and the meaning of the center-of-distances operator itself. Rewriting the question with those definitions included makes it sharp, stand-alone, and faithful to the paper’s intent without broadening it.
